People used to say the Tesla Semi is unreal, that Tesla won’t be able to hit the goals they aim for and blah blah blah.
But today is today.

WattEV just placed a $100 million order for 370 Tesla Semis, the largest single electric truck deployment in California history.

WattEV used to be one of Nikola’s biggest electric truck customers. They bought 36 Nikola Tre trucks. They ran them. Then Nikola filed for bankruptcy in February 2025.

WattEV took the lessons, ran a public RFP and chose Tesla.

~ 370 Tesla Semis 
~ $100 million 
~ Largest single electric truck order in California history 
~ 300+ going to the Port of Oakland 
~ Megawatt charging hubs in Oakland, Fresno, Stockton and Sacramento 
~ Full fleet by end of 2027

When the customer with the most direct experience comparing electric trucks in real freight operations picks Tesla, the market has chosen.

Tesla's ground testing engineering team is one of the hardcore teams at Tesla.

They test every vehicle in every kind of geography, weather and condition. Desert heat, Arctic cold, mountain passes, monsoon roads, midnight runs. Whatever the car will face in the real world, they put it through first.

It often means months away from family. Missed Christmases. Holidays spent in remote test sites instead of home. Birthdays celebrated over a phone call from a parking lot somewhere.

The reason your Tesla works the way it does in your driveway is because someone on this team already drove the same car somewhere harder.

If you look at the cost of solar power five years ago, 10 years ago, or 20 years ago, it would have seemed cost-prohibitive. But the cost of solar power today is extremely low.

The cost of batteries to store that energy has also dropped dramatically. Battery storage costs have fallen by a factor of 10 in the past five years.

So many of the studies that were done were done in times past, when batteries were very expensive and solar power was very expensive.

I would just encourage everyone to take another look at the cost of solar and the cost of batteries. I think you’ll find that you’re pleasantly surprised.

I flew my drone directly over Tesla’s Fremont Factory and captured something incredible:

The infamous Model 3 Tent — which has now become the Model Y Tent — where they complete final assembly of the Model Y after the battery and paint are done on the main line.

Even better? I tracked a completely empty Model 3 (no driver inside) as it autonomously drove itself from the charging station right after production all the way to the shipping yard.

This is real unsupervised FSD in action at the factory. Mind officially blown.
